subject: zoology_2
question_text: Explain Darwin's theory of Natural Selection with industrial melanism as an experimental proof.

steps.label: What the theory explains
steps.why: Natural selection needs no plan: whichever form survives better simply leaves more offspring.
common_mistakes: Saying the moths changed colour to match the trees. They did not; the proportions changed.
Confusing natural selection with Lamarck's use and disuse.
steps.memory_tip: Nature does not change the animal; it changes which animals survive.
steps.margin_note: One line on the theory before the example.
lines: explains how evolution might have occurred

steps.label: What industrial melanism is
steps.why: The soot changed the background the moths rest against, so the same colour that once hid a moth now showed it up.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the peppered moth by name.
Saying the pollution changed the moths' colour directly.
steps.memory_tip: Melanism means dark: the dark form is selected in polluted places.
steps.margin_note: Name the moth and the two colour forms.

steps.label: Before the revolution
steps.why: Against a pale lichen-covered bark, the grey moth was hidden and the black one stood out.
common_mistakes: Getting the direction wrong. Grey moths were abundant BEFORE the revolution.
Leaving out the birds, which do the selecting.
steps.margin_note: Say who does the selecting: the birds.

steps.label: After the revolution
steps.why: Nothing about either moth changed; only the background did, and that was enough to reverse which form survived.
common_mistakes: Saying the grey moths died out completely. They decreased in number.
Leaving out the soot on the tree bark.
steps.margin_note: End with the change in numbers. That is the proof.
